subject: sloth bear
title: A Bear Vacuums Up Termites So Loudly You Can Hear It 100 Meters Away

scenes.text: This bear is missing its two front teeth. That is not an accident.
The sloth bear of India and Sri Lanka weighs up to 140 kilos, and 95 percent of its diet, outside fruit season, is ants and termites.
It rips open a rock-hard termite mound with 8-centimeter claws, then presses its muzzle to the hole.
It shuts its nostrils so nothing crawls in, and sucks. The gap where its upper incisors should be turns its mouth into a vacuum nozzle.
The slurping is so loud it can be heard 100 meters away, about the length of a football pitch.
It is also the only bear that carries its cubs on its back, clinging to its shaggy fur for up to nine months. Missing teeth, built-in dust seal, and a free ride. One strange bear.

description:
Sloth bears of the Indian subcontinent weigh roughly 50 to 145 kg, and insects make up about 95 percent of their diet outside the fruiting season. Adults lack their two upper front incisors, leaving a gap that lets them suck up termites and ants, and they can close their nostrils completely to keep insects and dust out.
They tear open termite mounds with claws about 8 cm long, and their lips and tongue create a suction so loud it can be heard up to 100 metres away, according to the San Diego Zoo. Sloth bears are also the only bears that routinely carry their cubs on their backs, for up to 6 to 9 months.
